title: 2020 AMC 10B Problem 16
statement: Bela and Jenn play the following game on the closed interval \([0, n]\) of the real number line, where \(n\) is a fixed integer greater than \(4.\) They take turns playing, with Bela going first. At his first turn, Bela chooses any real number in the interval \([0, n].\) Thereafter, the player whose turn it is chooses a real number that is more than one unit away from all numbers previously chosen by either player. A player unable to choose such a number loses. Using optimal strategy, which player will win the game?

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: Bela will win if and only if \(n\) is odd.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: Jenn will win if and only if \(n\) is odd.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: Jenn will win if and only if \(n>8.\)

solutions.text:
Bela can first choose the midpoint \(\frac{n}{2}.\) After that, whenever Jenn chooses a number \(x,\) Bela chooses the reflected number \(n-x.\)

This reflected number is legal whenever Jenn’s move is legal: distances from previously chosen numbers are preserved by the reflection about \(\frac{n}{2},\) and Jenn cannot choose \(\frac{n}{2}\) because it was Bela’s first move. Therefore every Jenn move has a matching Bela response, so Jenn is the first player who can run out of legal moves.

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Look for a first move that leaves the interval symmetric
After Jenn moves to \(x,\) Bela can respond at \(n-x\)
